findings.title: `getCredentials` is not a `UserStorageProvider` or `CredentialInputValidator` method and violates the 4.8.3 compatibility contract of this test provider
findings.body: `BackwardsCompatibilityUserStorage` is specifically designed to simulate a legacy Keycloak 4.8.3 `UserStorageProvider` (which only implements `UserLookupProvider`, `UserStorageProvider`, `UserRegistrationProvider`, `CredentialInputUpdater`, `CredentialInputValidator`, and `UserQueryProvider`). However, `@Override public Stream<CredentialModel> getCredentials(RealmModel realm, UserModel user)` was added to it (along with `RecoveryAuthnCodesCredentialModel`, which did not exist in 4.8.3). A legacy user storage provider that only implements `CredentialInputUpdater`/`CredentialInputValidator` will not return `CredentialModel` instances from `user.credentialManager().getFederatedCredentialsStream()`, which instead queries `UserCredentialStore` (federated storage), not `UserStorageProvider`. If a real custom `UserStorageProvider` stores recovery codes via `updateCredential`, `RecoveryAuthnCodesUtils.getCredential(user)` will return `Optional.empty()`, causing `RecoveryAuthnCodeInputLoginBean` (line 19: `credentialModelOpt.get()`) to throw `NoSuchElementException` when rendering the recovery code login form.
